description: Sediment Strategy Seeks to Save Salt Marsh Species is a case study listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by USGS, United States Geological Survey; USFWS Seal Beach National Wildlife Refuge; Orange County Parks. One of Southern California’s few remaining tidal marshes (and the habitat it provides for marine life and endangered birds) is threatened by sea level rise. A collaborative effort is underway to help these wetlands stay above water. Coverage: California (2015). The toolkit gives California as the location, 2015 as the year. The listed link gives the documented application. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the cited source documents and the outcomes reported were not checked, and no model or dataset used was verified. It can support comparison with similar adaptation projects and planning precedents. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
